analysis.title: Prime Services Weekly Report, October 16, 2026 (Friday 10/9 – Thursday 10/15)
key_insights: GS Equity Fundamental L/S funds fell -1.68% between 10/9 and 10/15 versus MSCI World TR +0.05%, with alpha of -0.95% (long side losses) and beta of -0.74%.
GS Equity Systematic L/S funds fell -1.20% over the same period, with alpha of -1.78% from long and short side losses, partly offset by beta of +0.57%.

Overall book gross leverage rose 3.0 pts to 311.7% (79th percentile 1-year) while net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 72.7% (4th percentile 1-year). Overall L/S ratio fell 2.6% to 1.609 (4th percentile 1-year).
Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.4 pts to 210.9% (52nd percentile 1-year) and net leverage fell 4.2 pts to 48.6%, a 1-year low.
Global equities were net sold (-2.0 SDs 1-year). Gross trading activity fell at the fastest pace in nearly three months, with long sales outpacing short sales 2.6 to 1.

All major regions were net sold, led in dollar terms by EM Asia and North America. Single stocks made up most of the net selling, while macro products saw little net activity (long sales offset by short covers).
8 of 11 global sectors were net sold, led in dollar terms by Info Tech, Industrials and Consumer Discretionary. Health Care, Communication Services and Staples were the only net bought sectors.

Info Tech was the most net sold global sector, with the largest % de-grossing in 2 months and the largest % net selling on the desk's record (since 2016), driven by long sales and to a lesser extent short sales (4.7 to 1).

Info Tech was net sold and de-grossed in all major regions, led by EM Asia and North America. All subsectors except IT Services were net sold, led by Semis & Semi Equipment (long sales > short sales), Electronic Equipment (short sales > long sales) and Software (short sales > long sales).

The Prime book is now underweight Info Tech versus MSCI World by -8.4% (23rd percentile 1-year, 29th percentile 5-year). Gross/net allocations to Info Tech are 21.3%/23.5% of the global Prime book (48th percentile 1-year, 90th percentile 5-year).
Hedge funds net bought US Health Care at the fastest pace in 7 months while de-grossing the sector for a 5th straight week, with short covers outpacing long buys 2.2 to 1.

In US Health Care, all subsectors except Pharmaceuticals were net bought, led by Health Care Equipment & Supplies, Health Care Providers & Services (long buys > short covers) and Life Sciences Tools & Services (short covers > long buys). De-grossing was driven by Biotech short covers.
The Prime book is overweight US Health Care versus the S&P 500 by +10.9% (30th percentile 1-year, 86th percentile 5-year). Gross/net allocations are 15.4%/20.6% of US exposure.

The largest regional flow changes were in EM, with long sales of -2.35 SDs and short sales of -1.88 SDs. The largest sector flow changes were in Info Tech long sales (-2.61 SDs) and Real Estate short sales (-1.80 SDs).

sector_views.rationale: Prime book is underweight by -8.4% versus MSCI World after the largest net selling in the sector on the desk's record, led by semis and software.
Prime book is overweight US Health Care by +10.9% versus the S&P 500, with hedge funds net buying at the fastest pace in 7 months via short covers.

risk_factors: Long side losses drove Fundamental L/S alpha of -0.95%, and Systematic L/S lost on both long and short sides.
Concentrated de-grossing in Info Tech, led by semis, with EM Asia and North America most sold.
vol_and_positioning: Overall book net leverage at 72.7% is in the 4th percentile 1-year, and Fundamental L/S net leverage at 48.6% is a 1-year low (0th percentile).
Overall book gross leverage at 311.7% is in the 79th percentile 1-year and 96th percentile 5-year, against a T12M high of 322.9%.
Overall L/S ratio of 1.61 is in the 4th percentile 1-year and Fundamental L/S ratio of 1.64 is at the T12M low.
Global equities net selling of -2.0 SDs, with long sales outpacing short sales 2.6 to 1.
Info Tech saw the largest % de-grossing in 2 months and the largest % net selling on record since 2016.
HFs have de-grossed US Health Care for a 5th straight week while net buying it at the fastest pace in 7 months.
Market table: VIX 16.46 (+6.8% WoW), GS Most Short basket -3.7% WoW, GS VIP long basket -2.8% WoW, NYSE volume -25.3% WoW.
